'''''Conyza varia''''' is a species of flowering plants of the family [[Asteraceae]]. The species is endemic to [[Cape Verde]].<ref name=oromi>Oromí, Martín, Zurita & Cabrera, 2005 : ''[http://www.gobiernodecanarias.org/opencms8/export/sites/medioambiente/piac/galerias/descargas/Documentos/Publicaciones/Publicaciones-LPESCaboVerde.pdf Lista preliminar de especies silvestres de Cabo Verde: Hongos, Plantas y Animales Terrestres.]'' Gobierno de Canarias, Consejería de Medio Ambiente y Ordenación Territorial, p. 41</ref> It is listed as an endangered plant by the IUCN.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" /> First described as ''Erigeron varius'' by [[Philip Barker Webb]], it was placed in the genus ''Conyza'' by [[Hiram Wild]] in 1969. Its local name is ''marcelinha''<ref name=planta>[http://www.caboverde.com/nature/plan-09.jpg Plantas endémicas e arvores indígenas de Cabo Verde]</ref> or ''tabua'', ''tabuinha''. The plant plays a role in [[traditional medicine]]: crushed and heated leaves are used to treat external inflammations.<ref>{{cite web|author=Gomes, A.|author2=Vasconcelos, T.|author3=Almeida, H.|name-list-style=amp|title=Plantas na medicina tradicional de Cabo Verde|trans-title=Medicinal Traditional Plants in Cape Verde|language=pt|year=2008|url=http://www2.iict.pt/archive/doc/MH_Almeida_wrkshp_plts_medic.pdf|access-date=2016-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170329135958/http://www2.iict.pt/archive/doc/MH_Almeida_wrkshp_plts_medic.pdf|archive-date=2017-03-29}}</ref>

==Distribution and ecology==
''Conyza varia'' occurs in the island of [[Santo Antão, Cape Verde|Santo Antão]], [[São Vicente, Cape Verde|São Vicente]] (formerly), [[São Nicolau, Cape Verde|São Nicolau]], [[Santiago, Cape Verde|Santiago]], [[Fogo, Cape Verde|Fogo]] and [[Brava, Cape Verde|Brava]].<ref name="oromi"/>
